exposure: Early opioid administration at the ward-level
cohort: The study analyzed data from 111,693 patients in 392 surgical wards who were part of the German Quality Improvement in Postoperative Pain Management registry between 2010 and 2022.
finding: Patients treated on surgical wards with a higher rate of early opioid administration reported slightly better pain intensity and pain-related interference outcomes, but worse nausea outcomes, on the first postoperative day.
